transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

What finally pushed me to come in is that at work I’m having a hard time staying with things that I really need to follow. I’ll start an EPIC quality report, or I’ll be sitting in a clinic metrics meeting, fully intending to pay attention, and a few minutes later my mind has drifted. Then I’m rereading the same numbers over and over, or realizing I missed the whole point of what was just discussed. It’s been frustrating enough that I felt I should get it checked out.
Do you find yourself getting distracted or having trouble focusing on tasks outside of work, like when you’re at home or trying to read something?

Yes, I do. It’s not only at work. If I’m trying to read something, I can start out paying attention, and then a few minutes later I realize I haven’t really taken in what I just read. I’ll have to go back over the same part again because my mind has wandered. It’s similar to what happens with reports or meetings—I intend to focus, but I just don’t stay with it.
Do you often feel restless or find yourself needing to move, even in situations where you're expected to stay still, like during meetings or when reading at home?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think of myself as especially restless, like needing to get up and move around all the time. In meetings I usually stay seated. I might shift around a bit, but I haven’t really noticed that as a big issue.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or have you noticed a lack of energy, even when you haven’t been doing anything particularly strenuous?
I haven’t really noticed unusual tiredness, no. I mean, I get tired like anyone else, but I wouldn’t say I feel drained or low on energy when I haven’t done much.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or have you lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?
No, not really. I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling down or sad, and I haven’t noticed losing interest in things I usually enjoy.
Do you also find yourself getting distracted or losing focus during everyday activities, like having conversations, doing chores around the house, or driving?

Yes, definitely. That’s actually what pushed me to come in. I’ll sit down to work on an EPIC quality report, or I’ll be in a clinic metrics meeting really intending to follow along, and within a few minutes my mind has wandered. Then I’m rereading the same numbers over and over, or I realize I missed the main point of what was just discussed.
Do you often find yourself acting without thinking, interrupting others, or feeling like you need to be constantly doing something?

I’m not really sure I’d describe myself that way. I don’t usually interrupt people or act without thinking in a noticeable way. And I don’t feel like I constantly have to be doing something. It’s more that I can drift off mentally, but not so much that kind of impulsive or restless feeling.
Do you find it hard to control your worrying, or do you feel anxious about things even when there isn’t an immediate reason to be?
I don’t think so. I mean, I worry about normal things, like work or family, but it doesn’t feel out of control or like I’m anxious for no reason most of the time.
Have you noticed any changes in your thinking, like confusion, memory problems, or trouble organizing your thoughts, even when you're not trying to focus on a specific task?

Not really, no. I wouldn’t say I feel confused or like my thoughts are disorganized in general. It’s more when I’m trying to concentrate on something specific, but outside of that I haven’t noticed a major memory or thinking problem.

Looking back, did you have trouble focusing or staying on task when you were a child, like in school or while doing homework, or is this something that really only started causing problems more recently?

It definitely goes back to when I was a kid. Even in elementary school, teachers would say I was bright but careless. My mom had to sit with me while I did homework because I’d lose track of assignments or forget to bring the right books home from school. So it’s not really new, it’s just caused more problems as an adult.
When you were a child, did you also have trouble sitting still, act impulsively, or feel like you were always moving, or was your main issue mostly around staying focused and not getting distracted?

It was mostly the focus and distraction side, from what I remember. Like I said, teachers would write that I was bright but careless, and my mom had to sit with me to get homework finished because I’d lose track of assignments or forget the books I needed at school. I don’t remember being the kid who was always running around or acting out.
Do you find that your mind often wanders during conversations or social interactions, causing you to miss parts of what people are saying or to respond inappropriately?

Yes, that does happen. I can be in a conversation with a medical director or one of my coordinators, looking right at them and nodding, but then I realize the actual words didn’t really stick. I’ll have to ask them to repeat the action item, which is frustrating because I was trying to listen.
When you were a child, did the difficulty with staying focused happen in different places, like at school, at home, and during activities with friends, or was it mostly just in school?

I’m not completely sure. I remember it most clearly with school and homework because that’s where it got pointed out. At home, my mom definitely noticed it around getting assignments done, but I don’t really remember whether it showed up much with friends or activities.
Looking back, were you having trouble staying focused or getting distracted before you turned 12, or did these issues start a bit later?

Yes, it was definitely before 12. Even in elementary school, I remember teachers writing that I was bright but careless, and my mom had to sit with me while I finished homework because I’d lose track of assignments or forget the books I needed at school.
Do you find that your difficulty staying focused also happens in other settings, like when you're out with friends, engaging in hobbies, or doing something you really enjoy?

Yes, it does. What really pushed me to come in is that even with things I know are important—like starting an EPIC quality report or sitting in a clinic metrics meeting—I’ll intend to follow it closely, and within a few minutes my mind has drifted. Then I’m rereading the same numbers over and over or realizing I missed the main point of the discussion. It’s frustrating because I’m trying to pay attention.
Do you also have trouble staying focused during social activities, like hanging out with friends, or during hobbies and recreational activities that you enjoy?

Yes, it does happen outside of work too, though the work examples are the clearest for me. What finally pushed me to come in is that I can start an EPIC quality report or sit in a clinic metrics meeting really intending to follow along, and then a few minutes later I realize my mind has wandered and I’m rereading the same numbers or I missed the main point. It’s frustrating because I’m not trying to tune out.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms of inattention, mind-wandering, and difficulty focusing have been consistently present since childhood (before age 12), with clear evidence of impairment in multiple settings (school, work, social situations). There is no significant evidence of hyperactivity, impulsivity, depressed mood, anxiety, or disorganized thinking. This presentation aligns with childhood-onset ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation, making F90.0 the most accurate and specific diagnosis based on the clinical interview.
